clusters.name: your grandfather Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's collapse and death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her daughter Odette's every evening after work; your father Duncan took night shifts and distanced from Odette; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at the plant; Anton and Celeste separated; Odette's anxiety rose over her mother and Anton; your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. Your grandmother's functioning came back up in May 1979 when she took a job at the library.

clusters.name: your mother Odette's bed rest in pregnancy, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother Odette ordered to bed in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house, then argued with your father Duncan over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. These shifts pile up in the same months, all tied to the household under strain.

clusters.name: your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Your grandmother Hazel was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in September 1986. Within the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and all her appointments; your father Duncan phoned his father every night for news of her, then argued with Lyle over who should help their parents, and drank most evenings; Hazel had a bad fall and her functioning fell and rose with treatment; she could no longer dress herself and could no longer stand as her decline deepened; Odette took her to the clinic twice a week; Mavis came one week in four to nurse her sister; Duncan fought with Odette over his evenings at his parents' house; Ambrose gave up his workshop and hardly left Hazel's side. Hazel moved to the Fairlie nursing home in June 1997, where things settled.

clusters.name: your brother Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for the mines in May 1999: your father Duncan argued with Callum most nights over his plans to go north, then missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your mother Odette could not settle at the thought of Callum so far away; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; Odette took Ines with her everywhere, even to work. Your sister's functioning came back up by August 2000 when she returned to school full days and passed her exams.

clusters.name: your grandmother Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death at the Fairlie home in January 2003: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; your functioning came back up in November 2003 when you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again. These shifts are all yours in these months, and no one else's shows then.
